decision: Sendesis and ReasonHold are open-source products for other developers first; the author's projects are the first users, not the target.
rationale: Configuration must not assume one machine, one directory layout or one set of local services.
alternatives_considered: Build for the author's machines only

decision: ReasonHold is standalone (core library, CLI, MCP server) with an Agno integration package; Sendesis is built on Agno.
rationale: ReasonHold must serve users who do not use Agno; Sendesis gains Agno's agents, workflows, knowledge, tools and hooks.

decision: NVIDIA Switchyard is an optional transport only: a profile may point at a Switchyard or PAIR endpoint, and nothing in the core depends on it.
rationale: The Agno spike replaced Switchyard as the fabric; concepts shaped by the proxy (roles as routes, enforcement in the proxy) no longer hold.
alternatives_considered: Keep Switchyard as the routing fabric

decision: Sendesis v1 runs a full engineering team: design, plan, implement, verify, as a multi-model team under rules written in code.
rationale: Agno makes a much larger Sendesis possible than the review-loop-only plan.

decision: Human gates are configurable per workflow, with shipped defaults.
rationale: Different teams want different approval points; defaults keep the common case simple.

decision: Sendesis's interface is a CLI plus an MCP server.
rationale: The CLI serves batch jobs (qualify, gate); MCP serves use from inside Claude Code and Codex.

decision: The default workflow is Ariadne's governance workflow rebuilt as a multi-model Sendesis team; ReasonHold supplies its data and tools and ships a lighter single-agent skill pack.
rationale: The governance workflow is proven in Ariadne; rebuilding it as a team reuses that discipline.

decision: ReasonHold storage is re-tested in the ReasonHold spec; Auctor's Weaviate-only decision stands unless an embedded store passes the seven required capabilities.
rationale: Storage belongs to ReasonHold's own design; the ReasonHold spec later kept Weaviate.
alternatives_considered: Decide storage in the system vision

decision: The product supports any Agno model; 'cloud only through subscription CLIs, plus local' is the author's deployment rule, not a product rule.
rationale: An open-source product cannot impose one person's subscription setup.
alternatives_considered: Make the subscription-CLI rule a product rule

decision: Allowed client surfaces are claude -p, the Claude Agent SDK, codex exec and codex app-server, always with the CLI's own login state; no stored OAuth tokens.
rationale: The SDK and app-server give full tool loops and session resume while staying within the vendors' own clients.
alternatives_considered: Extract OAuth tokens for direct API use

decision: CLI-backed Agno models live in their own package, agno-cli-models, under Silicon-Wraith; Sendesis depends on it, and it may be offered to Agno upstream later.
rationale: The models are useful beyond Sendesis and have their own release cycle.

decision: Build order: agno-cli-models, then ReasonHold, then Sendesis.
rationale: Each later project depends on the earlier ones.

decision: Sendesis declares workflows that are compiled to Agno Workflow objects (approach A).
rationale: Declarative workflows stay reviewable and testable while Agno runs them.

decision: Qualification runs a role as a seat would run it, through the profile's Agno model class; the Phase 2 one-shot runners retire.
rationale: A receipt must describe the path production uses, not a separate harness.
alternatives_considered: Keep the Phase 2 subprocess runners for qualification

decision: The ReasonHold manifest is reasonhold.yaml for new projects; sync-doc.yaml is read as a legacy name.
rationale: A product-named manifest for new users without breaking Ariadne.
alternatives_considered: Keep sync-doc.yaml as the only name

decision: Decision record ids are derived deterministically from topic and datetime for existing records and written explicitly from now on.
rationale: Records need stable ids for supersedes_records and resolves without rewriting existing logs.
alternatives_considered: Rewrite existing logs to add ids

decision: Each project qualifies its own profiles; Sendesis does not ship receipts, it publishes gate reports as evidence.
rationale: Receipts depend on the user's models, CLIs and suites; shipped receipts would read UNKNOWN anywhere else.

decision: Run persistence uses SQLite by default, with Postgres as a supported option.
rationale: SQLite needs no service; Postgres serves teams that want a shared store.

decision: A run works in the worktree and branch it is started from.
rationale: A workflow run is already part of a feature's work on its own worktree; a second worktree would split the work.
alternatives_considered: Create a new worktree and branch per run

decision: Ungated cross-model loops are allowed with a prominent warning.
rationale: The operator prefers warnings over hard fails; the gate stays the evidence path.

decision: The plan gate is off by default.
rationale: Plans are reviewed by the operator before execution already; a default gate adds friction without new evidence.

decision: Worker roles without a suite are allowed as provisional, with a prominent warning.
rationale: Suites for every worker role do not exist yet; warnings keep the work moving while staying honest.

decision: docs/specs/2026-09-30-system-vision-design.md replaces docs/PLAN.md as the source of truth for scope and roadmap (spec section 12). PLAN.md stays as history; its capability ledger, suite and gate design, kill criteria and Spike 0 results remain valid.
rationale: The Agno spike changed the platform under the plan; the vision spec says PLAN.md is replaced once approved, and CLAUDE.md and README still point at the old design.

decision: Sendesis uses ReasonHold v0.1.1 for its own development: pinned dev dependency, reasonhold.yaml, decisions.jsonl, its own MCP server and SessionStart hook, and the skill pack. It reads ReasonHold and agno-cli-models read-only through local, uncommitted MCP entries, and writes only to its own logs.
rationale: Sendesis is where daily work happens, so it is where ReasonHold's skills, core library and MCP server get real use; read-only access to its two dependencies tests cross-project reading without breaking per-project ownership.
alternatives_considered: No ReasonHold in the Sendesis repo
Three read-write servers from one session

decision: M3 is one spec built in six stages (M3.1 to M3.6), each with its own plan, PR and exit criterion; checkpoint A is a real feature run end to end, exit B is team_gate reports for two review roles.
rationale: The stages share interfaces (schema v2 feeds the router, the router feeds the compiler); one spec keeps them consistent while each stage stays reviewable.

decision: Sendesis tests in three tiers: unit with a scripted fake Agno model (every run), local models through Agno's own classes (marker local, free), and subscription CLIs (marker integration, spends quota).
rationale: Control flow needs scripted outputs; local models prove real integration without quota; the CLI tier covers auth, isolation and sandboxing.
alternatives_considered: Local models instead of the fake model in unit tests

decision: Every role without a qualification suite runs as provisional with a prominent warning, reviewers included; M3 builds the Code Reviewer suite; executable suites for the Implementer and Test Engineer come after M3.
rationale: Reaches the dogfood checkpoint without building suites for every role, while gate evidence covers two review roles.

decision: Schema validity is judged on its point value (at least 0.98 after one retry); recall and false positives stay at the Wilson lower bound. A label may carry several acceptable ranges, and several findings for one label count as one hit.
rationale: 100 of 100 valid gives a Wilson lower bound of 0.963, so 0.98 at the bound needs about 189 outputs; schema validity is a hygiene check. Correct findings at a sink were scored as misses.

decision: Edit and shell seats run autonomously with no per-call approvals and no network for the model's own commands, both families sandboxed alike; a workflow stage may grant a recorded loopback-only allowance. ReasonHold tools run in Sendesis's process outside the sandbox.
rationale: Matches Codex's workspace-write sandbox and keeps the families equal for diversity and qualification; stage commits, resets and gates are the human checkpoints.

decision: A feature run starts from --request or --brief at Design, or from an approved --design at Plan (the skip recorded as a decision); the interactive Clarify stage is deferred to a later release, if ever.
rationale: The operator designs in conversation already; a relayed clarify loop adds latency and machinery for little gain now.

decision: Stage skips come only from the CLI (run --skip or a gate answer), require a reason, state what the skip loses, and are recorded as human decisions with the run id; Orient and Final are never skippable.
rationale: Preserves Ariadne's operator-only bypass; MCP callers are agents.

decision: Only confirmed findings send work back; a disputed blocking finding goes to the top of the operator's next gate; findings whose evidence fails mechanical verification are kept but never block.
rationale: Loops stay cheap and cannot be dragged by one model's false positive, and nothing blocking is silently dropped.
alternatives_considered: Any blocking finding with valid evidence loops

decision: Sendesis has ten roles: the Code Validator reviews the contract (code against design and assertions) and the Code Reviewer reviews correctness and standards; the new suite belongs to the Code Reviewer.
rationale: Clean scopes per role, and the planted-bug suite measures correctness, not contract adherence.

decision: Stage order is Verify, then Doc sync limited to factual drift (never specs, plans or architecture; design claims become findings), then Final, with the Doc Syncer's diff shown separately.
rationale: Verify keeps judging code against the approved design; a limited Syncer cannot launder a bug into the documentation.
alternatives_considered: An extra review seat for the Syncer's diff

decision: Implement runs a per-task inner loop: the tests the plan names, then one Code Validator of another family checks the task's diff against its Design Assertions; up to 3 fix rounds, then escalation. Designs must have a Design assertions section and every plan task an assertions block.
rationale: Ariadne's Gate 1: skipping the per-task assertion check is how the chunker's Weaviate writes survived.

decision: Reviewers receive evidence packs built by Sendesis's code (diff, files in scope, test results, ReasonHold inventories) plus exact-query tools; could-not-run is never read as a pass; absence claims require complete inventories.
rationale: Review roles have no shell; command-derived evidence must come from code.

decision: Seats never call store_decision; Sendesis's own code writes decisions to ReasonHold only when the operator approves at a gate.
rationale: Keeps Gate 2's 'recorded at approval time' true and stops agents recording unreviewed decisions.

decision: Gate runs pause on a rate limit and resume later instead of failing over; they are resumable and may spread over days.
rationale: Substituting a profile mid-gate would change what an arm measures; the pilot alone is about 3,000 CLI calls.

decision: README sections Model Routing and Local and Distributed Inference are rewritten for the Agno design: the router picks among model classes, Switchyard and PAIR are optional transports, local models are openai_like profiles.
rationale: Both sections were retracted by vision-spec-replaces-plan-md until rewritten; M3.1 rewrites them as the M3 spec's section 11 requires.

The two README retractions are resolved by the rewrite recorded in readme-routing-sections-rewritten.
rationale: The README sections were rewritten in M3.1, so only the four docs/PLAN.md retractions remain.

decision: Qualification scores only measured cases. A case whose final outcome is TIMEOUT, ERROR, or STALL after its retry is unmeasured: it counts neither as a miss nor as clean, the receipt records n_measured and the unmeasured case ids with their outcomes, and any unmeasured case keeps the receipt UNKNOWN.
rationale: In the M3.1 exit run five Codex stream stalls counted as misses and printed recall 0.677 FAIL, a measurement that never happened. A receipt must never reach QUALIFIED or FAILED on a subset of the suite.
alternatives_considered: Drop unmeasured cases and allow QUALIFIED on the rest
session_context: Codex stream stalls in the M3.1 exit run; docs/specs/2026-10-01-codex-stall-handling-design.md

decision: The idle limit lives in agno-cli-models and is measured on CLI protocol messages, not only on the events Agno sees. Sendesis sets it per profile (optional idle_timeout_s, part of the profile hash) and maps the resulting CliStallError to Outcome.STALL. The wall-clock limit stays.
rationale: Only agno-cli-models sees every app-server message, including reasoning, which Agno's events do not cover. One wall-clock limit cannot tell slow from stalled; the stalls cost about 300 s each when about 60 s is enough.
alternatives_considered: Idle limit in Sendesis on Agno events
Rely on Codex's own stream_idle_timeout_ms (override for the built-in provider unverified)
session_context: Codex stream stalls in the M3.1 exit run; docs/specs/2026-10-01-codex-stall-handling-design.md

decision: A STALL gets one retry in qualification, like INVALID, with both attempts logged. In runs, STALL is a failover trigger like TIMEOUT but does not skip the profile for the rest of the run the way a rate limit does. TIMEOUT and ERROR get no retry in qualification.
rationale: The five stalled cases all passed on rerun, so a retry is evidence-backed for stalls only.
session_context: Codex stream stalls in the M3.1 exit run; docs/specs/2026-10-01-codex-stall-handling-design.md

decision: Request to agno-cli-models (pending): (1) add idle_timeout_s: float | None to CliModel; when set, a call that receives no message from the CLI for that long raises CliStallError. (2) CliStallError is a new public subclass of CliTimeoutError carrying idle_s, last_method (the last protocol message's method) and answer_open (whether a final-answer item was open). (3) Codex: the idle clock resets on every message from codex app-server (item/started, deltas, token updates, everything read by Rpc._read), not only on the ModelResponse events _timed sees; default 60 s. (4) Claude Code: default None until its event cadence is measured (see request-agno-cli-models-substrate-checks). (5) idle_timeout_s is part of config_fingerprint() for both classes. (6) The wall-clock timeout_s stays unchanged. (7) Tests with a fake app-server that opens an agentMessage item and goes silent (raises CliStallError within the idle limit), one that pauses below the limit between events (does not trip), and the wall clock still firing on a slow but chatty stream. (8) README Isolation/Errors sections updated; released as a tag Sendesis can pin.
rationale: Sendesis needs stalls detected in about 60 s and typed separately from slow calls (decisions idle-limit-upstream, stall-is-not-a-miss). Only agno-cli-models sees every protocol message. Evidence: reports/2026-10-01-m3.1-exit-run.md and docs/specs/2026-10-01-codex-stall-handling-design.md in Sendesis (PR #4).

decision: Request to agno-cli-models (pending): two measurements, reported back as decisions in agno-cli-models. (1) Claude Agent SDK message cadence: the longest silence between SDK messages in healthy runs at effort high, including long thinking, so a Claude idle default can be set from data. (2) Whether Codex's per-provider stream_idle_timeout_ms and stream_max_retries (present in codex-cli 0.155.1 under ModelProviderInfo) can be overridden for the built-in ChatGPT provider through -c on codex app-server, and whether a reconnect is visible in app-server notifications.
rationale: The stall design refuses to set a Claude idle default by analogy with Codex, and rejected Codex's own reconnect only because the override is unverified. Evidence: reports/2026-10-01-m3.1-exit-run.md and docs/specs/2026-10-01-codex-stall-handling-design.md in Sendesis (PR #4).

decision: Request to agno-cli-models (pending): Codex isolation does not remove everything user-level. In the M3.1 exit run every codex app-server call received the user's global skills block (<skills_instructions> from ~/.codex/skills), a multi-agent developer prompt ('You are /root, the primary agent in a team of agents' plus a <multi_agent_mode> block), and ran with features including Collab, SleepTool, CodexHooks, ShellSnapshot and memories-related state. Disable these through FIXED_CONFIG or thread/start parameters where Codex allows it, document what cannot be disabled, and include the change in config_fingerprint().
rationale: Anything the user installs globally changes what the model sees during qualification, which a receipt cannot certify. Evidence: ~/.codex/sessions rollouts from 2026-10-01 21:14 to 21:52 UTC; Codex log feedback_tags features list. Evidence: reports/2026-10-01-m3.1-exit-run.md and docs/specs/2026-10-01-codex-stall-handling-design.md in Sendesis (PR #4).

decision: Request to agno-cli-models (pending): (1) export CliModel from the package root so Sendesis and its tests stop importing agno_cli_models._base.CliModel; (2) add claude CLI 2.1.287 to the tested set after a test run on it (Sendesis pins 2.1.287; every call currently warns UnsupportedCliVersionWarning).
rationale: Found in Sendesis M3.1's final review and exit run. Evidence: reports/2026-10-01-m3.1-exit-run.md and docs/specs/2026-10-01-codex-stall-handling-design.md in Sendesis (PR #4).
